content.text:
I submitted index 0 (Sb fraction 0.211) as the best composition, but I didn't find a working photoanode: every EQE reading was close to zero. Index 0 was the only positive reading, at 0.00025%, and that is too small to count as real activity.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.211 | +0.00025 |
| 6 | 0.360 | −0.00001 |
| 11 | 0.517 | −0.00312 |
| 16 | 0.685 | −0.00037 |
| 22 | 0.832 | −0.00163 |

- **Search pattern:** I spent three measurements across the middle of the line first. The spot near the known CuSb₂O₆ composition (Sb fraction 0.667) was one of them. All three read zero, so I used the last two on the two ends.
- **XRD at the Sb-rich end (index 24):** the pattern matches Sb₂O₄ best (similarity 0.79). That oxide has a wide band gap and shouldn't absorb light at the stated 2.1 eV, which fits the zero reading at index 22.
- **XRD at the Cu-rich end (index 1):** the best match was CuSb₂O₆, but only at 0.51. The low-angle peaks point to a second Cu-rich phase with a large unit cell that none of the listed structures explain. I didn't measure the lowest-Sb compositions beyond index 0, so that end is the least ruled out.

**Budget:** all 5 EQE measurements are used; 3 of the 5 XRD measurements were left over.

Only 5 of the 30 compositions were measured, so I can't rule out a narrow active spot between them, for example between Sb fractions 0.23 and 0.33. The GP suggestion tool was never used. If the whole line really is inactive under these conditions, any pick scores about the same.
